en: I will follow your orders...
I've been terribly tired lately, you know.
Give me any order.
Delivering letters is my job...
Oh, so you're a mail carrier.
That's right.
But I can't take mail from you right now, so
go to the post office or drop it in a postbox.
Are you on your way to work too?
Oh,
Would you like to help me with my work now?
Oh, I'm only joking.
My job is delivering letters.
Actually, I'm not going to work now,
I'm on my way home.
Are you, too?
We really do run into each other a lot.
Do you live nearby?
I deliver letters for a living.
If you have a letter you want delivered,
please come to the post office.
It's a bit of a problem if you come to me.
please take it to the post office or a postbox.
You always dress so flashily.
I'd love to try wearing clothes like that.
Where do you get your clothes made?
I'd like you to introduce me to that shop.
come and visit again.
You've come already.
You're more impatient than I expected.
Hello. This is the post office.
Any letter you leave with us,
we deliver from the European countryside

variants.en: We deliver from the European countryside

en: to cities all over the world.
Cities all over the world...?
Yes. How many days it takes depends on the place,
but we deliver anywhere.
Oh, we met the other day...
This is the post office counter.
If you have any mail you'd like delivered,
please bring it in any time.
Next, please.
I'd like to ask you something,
how long does it take for mail
to be delivered?
Let me see...
Letters are mostly carried by carriage
to their destination.
But we have the railway now,
so letters quickly reach
any city.
Things have become so convenient, haven't they?
Ah, but for cities that need a ship,
it takes a little longer.
(Orgo can fly, so
it may well be the better one.)
Did you know?
England has something called the telegraph,
and you can get a message across without
delivering a letter by hand, I hear.
About that mess... I mean, telegraph,
could you tell me a little more?
I don't know the details myself, but
apparently the letter is first turned
into an electric signal.
Then it's turned back into a letter at the other end.
It really has become a convenient world.
(It may be more useful than Orgo.)
England has something called the telephone,
which lets people talk directly, even when
they're far apart, I hear.
What an amazing world we live in.
(If that can be done, there's no point in sending
a familiar off just to carry a message.)
If this telephone thing becomes widespread,
will I end up out of work?
Even a convenient world isn't always
a good thing, is it.
(That's just what Orgo says...)
